4052: ###### 3.3.2.2.2. Characteristics
4053: 
4054: There are two LE advertising physical channels: the primary advertising physical channel and the secondary advertising physical channel.
4055: 
4056: The primary advertising physical channel is a set of three fixed PHY channels spread evenly across the LE frequency spectrum. The number of primary advertising PHY channels can be reduced by the advertising device in order to reduce interference. The primary advertising physical channel can use either the LE 1M or LE Coded PHY.
4057: 
4058: The primary advertising physical channel is divided into advertising events where each advertising event can hop on all primary advertising PHY channels. The advertising events occur at regular intervals which are slightly modified with a random delay to aid in interference avoidance.
4059: 
4060: On the primary advertising physical channel the advertising device controls access to the physical channel. The advertising device starts its transmission in an advertising event and transmits advertising packets on one or more of the primary advertising PHY channels. Each advertising packet is sent on a different advertising PHY channel at a fixed interval. Seven types of advertising events can be used, with each advertising event type having different sized advertising packets. The PDU payloads of these advertising packets can vary in length from 6 to 37 octets.
4061: 
4062: Some advertising events sent by the advertising device permit the listening device to concurrently send scan requests or connection requests packets on the same advertising PHY channel in which the advertising packet was received. The advertising device can send a scan response packet again on the same advertising PHY channel within the same advertising event. The payload of the scan response packet can vary in length from 6 to 37 octets.
4063: 
4064: The secondary advertising physical channel is a set of 37 fixed PHY channels spread across the LE frequency spectrum. These are the same fixed LE PHY channels used by the data physical channel. The secondary advertising physical channel uses the same channel indices as the data physical channel. The payload of advertising packets used on the secondary advertising physical channel can vary in length from 0 to 255 octets. Advertising packets on the secondary advertising physical channel are not part of the advertising event but are part of the extended advertising event. These extended advertising events begin at the same time as the advertising event on the primary advertising physical channel and conclude with the last packet on the secondary advertising physical channel.
4065: 
4066: The secondary advertising physical channel is used to offload data that would otherwise be transmitted on the primary advertising physical channel. Advertising packets on the secondary advertising physical channel ("auxiliary packets") are scheduled by the advertiser when sufficient over-the-air time is available. The advertising packet on the primary advertising physical channel contains the PHY channel and the offset to the start time of the auxiliary packet.
4067: 
4068: The secondary advertising physical channel can use any LE PHY. All advertising packets on the secondary advertising physical channel in the same extended advertising event use the same PHY, which is specified in the advertising packet on the primary advertising physical channel.
4069: 
4070: ###### 3.3.2.2.3. Topology
4071: 
4072: An LE advertising physical channel can be shared by any number of LE devices. Any number of LE devices can transmit advertising packets while sharing the advertising physical channel. Any number of scanning devices can listen on the advertising physical channel. An advertising device can advertise and be connected on an LE piconet physical channel simultaneously. Scanning devices may also be connected to one or more LE piconet physical channels simultaneously.
4073: 
4074: ###### 3.3.2.3. Periodic physical channel
4075: 
4076: ###### 3.3.2.3.1. Overview
4077: 
4078: An LE periodic physical channel is used to set up a periodic broadcast between unconnected devices.
4079: 
4080: ###### 3.3.2.3.2. Characteristics
4081: 
4082: The periodic physical channel is characterized by a pseudo-random sequence of PHY channels and additional parameters provided by the advertiser. These are the channel map that indicates the set of PHY channels used in the periodic broadcast, the event counter used to determine the channel hopping sequence, the offset indicating the timing of the first periodic broadcast packet, and the interval between successive periodic broadcasts.
4083: 
4084: The channel is divided into periodic advertising events where the start of a periodic advertising event corresponds to a PHY hop channel. The start of consecutive periodic advertising events corresponds to different PHY hop channels. The first packet sent by the advertiser after the broadcast is established sets an anchor point for the timing of all future periodic advertising events.
4085: 
4086: On the periodic physical channel, the advertising device controls access to the physical channel. The advertiser starts its transmission in a periodic advertising event that occurs at regular intervals. Packets transmitted by the advertiser are aligned with the periodic advertising event and specified broadcast timing. Additional packets may also be transmitted between the periodic advertising events. The payload of packets sent by the advertiser may vary in length from 0 octets to 255 octets.
4087: 
4088: Each advertiser transmission contains a packet carrying information on the PADVB logical transports. Scanners cannot transmit on the physical channel.
4089: 
4090: There are 37 PHY channels. The advertiser can reduce this number through the channel map indicating the used channels. When the hopping pattern hits an unused channel, the unused channel is replaced with an alternate from the set of used channels. The periodic physical channel can use any PHY. All periodic advertising events use the same PHY used by the advertiser in the packet describing the characteristics of the periodic physical channel.
4091: 
4092: ###### 3.3.2.3.3. Topology
4093: 
4094: An LE periodic physical channel can be shared by any number of LE devices. Any number of LE devices can transmit periodic advertising packets while sharing the same periodic physical PHY channels. Any number of scanning devices can listen on the periodic physical channel. An advertising device can advertise and be synchronized on an LE periodic physical channel simultaneously. Scanning devices may also be synchronized to one or more LE periodic physical channels simultaneously.
4095: 
4096: ###### 3.3.2.4. LE Isochronous physical channel
4097: 
4098: The LE isochronous physical channel can be created to transfer isochronous data between LE devices.
4099: 
4100: ###### 3.3.2.4.1. Overview
4101: 
4102: The LE isochronous physical channel is used to transfer isochronous data between connected or unconnected LE devices.
4103: 
4104: ###### 3.3.2.4.2. Characteristics
4105: 
4106: The LE isochronous physical channel is characterized by a pseudo-random sequence of PHY channels and by three additional parameters that are provided by a Central or a connectionless broadcaster. The first parameter is the channel map that indicates the set of PHY channels. The second parameter is a pseudo random number that is used as an index into the complete set of PHY channels. The third parameter is the timing of the first data packet. The timing of the first packet of a CIS is provided in the Link Layer message that is sent in the associated ACL connection by the Central during the CIS establishment phase. The timing of the first packet of a BIS is referenced from a periodic advertising event associated with the BIS.
4107: 
4108: The LE isochronous physical channel is used to transfer isochronous data in isochronous events that occur at regular intervals. Each isochronous event is divided into one or more subevents. Each subevent uses a PHY channel that is selected by the channel selection algorithm.
4109: 
4110: In any subevent in an isochronous connection, the Central transmits a packet to the Peripheral and the Peripheral may respond with a packet of its own. The Central controls the access to the LE isochronous physical channel. In every CIS event, the Central starts its transmission at the start of the first subevent. Packets that are transmitted by the Central are time aligned with the start of every subevent.
4111: 
4112: A Broadcasting Isochronous transmitter transmits isochronous data packets and control packets. Any device that is synchronized to the BIS can receive these packets. The broadcasting device controls access to the LE isochronous physical channel. Within BIS events, the broadcasting device starts its transmission in the first subevent. Packets that are transmitted by the broadcasting device are aligned with the start of every subevent.
4113: 
4114: There are 37 PHY channels. The Central or the isochronous stream transmitter can reduce this number through the channel map that indicates the used channels. When the channel selection algorithm selects an unused channel, the unused channel is replaced with an alternate from the set of used channels. For CISes, the LE isochronous physical channel uses the set of PHY channels that are enabled on the LE piconet physical channel. The LE isochronous physical channel can use any LE PHY.
4115: 
4116: ###### 3.3.2.4.3. Topology
4117: 
4118: The LE isochronous physical channel in a CIS can be used for one-to-one communication between the devices that are in the LE piconet. The Central may establish one or more CISes with the Peripheral in the LE piconet; that is, the LE isochronous physical channel can carry one or more CIS logical transports between a given Central and Peripheral. The LE isochronous physical channel and all the CISes it carries are terminated when the associated LE piconet physical channel is terminated. If a Central has established piconets with more than one Peripheral, it can establish LE isochronous physical channels with more than one of these Peripherals at the same time.
4119: 
4120: The LE isochronous physical channel can be used for one-to-many communication topologies of unconnected LE devices. Each LE isochronous physical channel can carry one or more BIS logical transports.
4121: 
4122: ###### 3.3.2.5. LE Channel Sounding physical channel
4123: 
4124: The LE CS physical channel can be created to transfer time and phase information that can be used to generate a distance estimate.
4125: 
4126: ###### 3.3.2.5.1. Overview
4127: 
4128: An LE CS physical channel is used to exchange time-interleaved modulated tones and packets that allow a pair of devices to measure the time of flight, amplitude, and phase of signals sent over the communication channel. This information can be used to estimate the distance between two LE devices.
4129: 
4130: ###### 3.3.2.5.2. Characteristics
4131: 
4132: The LE CS physical channel is characterized by a pre-negotiated sequence of exchanges that make up a CS procedure. Characteristics and content of these exchanges is derived from the output of a Deterministic Random Bit Generator (DRBG). The DRBG is used to generate the content of the CS Access Address and payload content. It is also used to influence the modulated content of tone transmissions. Finally, the DRBG is used to seed the selection of the pseudo-random sequence of the PHY channels used in the channel hop sequence of a Channel Sounding procedure.
4133: 
4134: The duration of a CS procedure is determined by the time it takes for a predetermined number of CS steps to be exchanged. Additional time may be required to partition the CS steps into subevents in order to coexist with other activities using the same radio or spectrum.
4135: 
4136: CS steps are defined as a bidirectional exchange between initiator and reflector devices. These steps are further aggregated into a related timing group known as a CS subevent. These subevents are timed from an offset of the underlying LE piconet physical channel connection event anchor point. A CS event is defined as the group of all CS subevents offset from the same LE piconet physical channel connection event anchor point.
4137: 
4138: Each step exchange may include a modulated packet, a modulated tone, or both. The initiator device transmits first, followed by at least one transmission from the reflector. A modulated tone may be transmitted more than once in each direction in cases where multiple antenna paths are employed.
4139: 
4140: ###### 3.3.2.5.3. Topology
4141: 
4142: An LE Channel Sounding physical channel is used for one-to-one communication between two devices that are in the same piconet, where one is in the initiator role and the other is in the reflector role. In the context of CS, an initiator is the device that starts the CS procedure, and a reflector is the device that responds. The procedure’s operating parameters are exchanged in Link Layer control messages. LE CS physical channel timing depends on the timing of the initiator device, which is followed by the reflector device. The LE Central device may assume either the initiator or reflector role. Likewise, the LE Peripheral device may assume either role.
4143: 
4144: An LE device can use only one LE Channel Sounding physical channel at a time. To support multiple concurrent Channel Sounding operations, the device uses time-division multiplexing between multiple LE Channel Sounding physical channels, which allows a device to appear to support multiple connected devices with Channel Sounding physical channels.
4145: 
4146: ###### 3.3.3. \[This section is no longer used\]
4147: 
4148: ##### 3.4. Physical links
4149: 
4150: A physical link represents a baseband connection between Bluetooth devices. A physical link is always associated with exactly one physical channel (although a physical channel may support more than one physical link). Within the Bluetooth system a physical link is a virtual concept that has no direct representation within the structure of a transmitted packet.
4151: 
4152: In BR/EDR the access code packet field, together with the clock and address of the Central Bluetooth device, is used to identify a physical channel. In LE, the access address and channel map, including *hopIncrement* in the case of Channel Selection Algorithm #1 or an event counter in the case of Channel Selection Algorithm #2, are used to identify a physical channel. For BR/EDR and LE, there is no subsequent part of the packet that directly identifies the physical link. Instead, the physical link may be identified by association with the logical transport, as each logical transport is only received on one physical link.
4153: 
4154: Some physical link types have properties that may be modified. An example of this is the transmit power for the link. Other physical link types have no modifiable properties. In the case of BR/EDR physical links with modifiable properties the LM protocol is used to adapt these properties. In the case of LE physical links with modifiable properties the LL protocol is used to adapt these properties. As the LM protocol (BR/EDR) or LL protocol (LE) is supported at a higher layer (by a logical link) the appropriate physical link is identified by implication from the logical link that transports the LM or LL signaling.
4155: 
4156: In the situation where a transmission is broadcast over a number of different physical links, then the transmission parameters are selected to be suitable for all of the physical links.
4157: 
4158: ###### 3.4.1. BR/EDR links supported by the basic and adapted piconet physical channels
4159: 
4160: The basic piconet physical channel supports a physical link which may only be active. The adapted piconet physical channel may support several physical links, including active and Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast. An active physical link is a point-to-point link between the Central and a Peripheral. A Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast physical link is a point-to-multipoint link between the Transmitter (Central) and zero or more Receivers (Peripherals). At least one physical link on the piconet physical channel is always present when a Peripheral is synchronized in the piconet.
4161: 
4162: ###### 3.4.1.1. Active physical link
4163: 
4164: The physical link between a Central and a Peripheral is active if a default ACL logical transport exists between the devices. Active physical links have no direct identification of their own, but are identified by association with the default ACL logical transport ID with which there is a one-to-one correspondence.
4165: 
4166: An active physical link has the associated property of radio transmit power in each direction. Transmissions from Peripherals are always directed over the active physical link to the Central, and use the transmit power that is a property of this link in the Peripheral to Central direction. Transmissions from the Central may be directed over a single active physical link (to a specific Peripheral) or over a number of physical links (to a group of Peripherals in the piconet). In the case of point-to-point transmissions the Central uses the appropriate transmit power for the physical link in question. (In the case of point-to-multipoint transmissions the Central uses a transmit power appropriate for the set of devices addressed.)
4167: 
4168: Active physical links may be placed into Hold or Sniff mode. The effect of these modes is to modify the periods when the physical link is active and may carry traffic. Logical transports that have defined scheduling characteristics are not affected by these modes and continue according to their pre-defined scheduling behavior. The default ACL logical transport and other links with undefined scheduling characteristics are subject to the mode of the active physical link.
4169: 
4170: ###### 3.4.1.2. \[This section is no longer used\]
4171: 
4172: ###### 3.4.1.3. Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast physical link
4173: 
4174: A Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast physical link is present on a Receiver (Peripheral) when it is synchronized in the piconet where a CPB logical transport exists. On a Transmitter (Central), a Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast physical link is present when a CPB logical transport exists whether or not any Receivers are synchronized. The Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast physical link is a point-to-multipoint unidirectional link between a Transmitter and zero or more Receivers.
4175: 
4176: Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast physical links do not support power control because there is no feedback from Receivers to the Transmitter. Traffic is always directed from a single Transmitter to zero or more Receivers.
4177: 
4178: Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast packets are sent at regular intervals. The BR/EDR Controller selects an interval within a range requested by the Host.
4179: 
4180: ###### 3.4.2. BR/EDR links supported by the scanning physical channels
4181: 
4182: In the case of inquiry scan and page scan channels, the physical link exists for a relatively short time and cannot be controlled or modified in any way. These types of physical links are not further elaborated.
4183: 
4184: ###### 3.4.3. LE links supported by the LE physical channels
4185: 
4186: The LE piconet physical channels support an LE active physical link. The physical link is a point-to-point link between the Central and a Peripheral. It is always present when the Peripheral is in a connection with the Central.
4187: 
4188: The LE advertising physical channels support an LE advertising physical link. The physical link is a broadcast between the advertiser device and one or more scanner or initiator devices. It is always present when the advertiser is broadcasting advertisement events.
4189: 
4190: The LE periodic physical channels support an LE periodic physical link. The physical link is a broadcast between the advertiser device and one or more scanner devices. It is always present when the advertiser is broadcasting periodic advertising events.
4191: 
4192: The LE isochronous physical channels support LE isochronous physical links. An LE isochronous physical link can be a point-to-point link between a Central and a Peripheral or a connectionless link between a broadcast isochronous transmitter and multiple receiving devices.
4193: 
4194: ###### 3.4.3.1. Active physical link
4195: 
4196: The physical link between a Central and a Peripheral is active if a default LE ACL logical transport exists between the devices. Active physical links are each associated with a separate piconet physical channel, which in turn is identified by the randomly generated Access Address used in the Link Layer packet. Each Access Address has a one-to-one relationship with the Central and the Peripheral of the active physical link.
4197: 
4198: An active physical link has the associated property of radio transmit power in each direction, which may be different in each direction. A device uses the appropriate transmit power for the physical link in question.
4199: 
4200: ###### 3.4.3.2. Advertising physical link
4201: 
4202: An advertising physical link between an advertising device and an initiating device for the purposes of forming a connection (active physical link) can exist for a relatively short period of time. These advertising physical links cannot be controlled or modified in any way and these types of physical links are not further elaborated.
4203: 
4204: An advertising physical link between an advertising device and a scanning device used for periodic broadcasting of user data can exist for longer periods of time. There is no identification information about the physical link within the protocol. The relationship between the advertising and scanning device is established through the use of the Bluetooth Device Address.
4205: 
4206: ###### 3.4.3.3. Periodic physical link
4207: 
4208: A periodic physical link between an advertising device and one or more scanning devices normally exists for a prolonged period of time. Periodic physical links are each associated with a separate periodic physical channel, which in turn is identified by the randomly generated Access Address used in the Link Layer packet. Each Access Address has a one-to-one relationship with the advertiser of the periodic physical link.
4209: 
4210: ###### 3.4.3.4. Isochronous physical links
4211: 
4212: The isochronous physical link uses an isochronous physical channel and carries CIS and BIS logical transports.
4213: 
4214: Isochronous physical links carrying CIS(es) use the appropriate transmit power level for the physical link in question. Devices use power control on the associated ACL-C logical link to adapt the transmit power level for the physical link.
4215: 
4216: Isochronous physical links carrying BIS(es) do not support power control because there is no feedback from Observers to the Broadcaster. Traffic is always directed from a single Broadcaster to zero or more Observers.
4217: 
4218: ###### 3.4.3.5. Channel Sounding physical link
4219: 
4220: Channel Sounding procedures exist within an LE Channel Sounding physical link and are characterized by their transitory existence as well as their unique timing characteristics relative to an LE active physical link. Channel Sounding procedures are based on a preexisting LE active physical link. A CS procedure’s start timing is also dependent on the timing of the corresponding LE active physical link.
4221: 
4222: A Channel Sounding physical channel supports a Channel Sounding physical link.
4223: 
4224: ###### 3.4.4. \[This section is no longer used\]

4226: ##### 3.5. Logical links and logical transports
4227: 
4228: A variety of logical links are available to support different application data transport requirements. Each logical link is associated with a logical transport, which has a number of characteristics. These characteristics include flow control, acknowledgment/repeat mechanisms, sequence numbering and scheduling behavior. Logical transports are able to carry different types of logical links (depending on the type of the logical transport). In the case of some of the Bluetooth logical links these are multiplexed onto the same logical transport. Logical transports may be carried by active physical links on either the basic or the adapted piconet physical channel.
4229: 
4230: Logical transport identification and real-time (link control) signaling are carried in the packet header, and for some logical links identification is carried in the payload header. Control signaling that does not require single slot response times is carried out using the LMP protocol.

4365: The classification of each link type follows from a selection procedure within three categories.

4367: ###### 3.5.1. Casting
4368: 
4369: The first category is that of casting. This may be either unicast or broadcast.
4370: 
4371: -   Unicast links exist between exactly two endpoints. Traffic may be sent in either direction on unicast links.
4372:     
4373: -   Broadcast links exist between one source device and zero or more receiver devices. Traffic is unidirectional, i e., only sent from the source devices to the receiver devices. Broadcast links are connectionless, meaning there is no procedure to create these links, and data may be sent over them at any time. Broadcast links are unreliable, and there is no guarantee that the data will be received.
4374:     
4375: 
4376: ###### 3.5.2. Scheduling and acknowledgment scheme
4377: 
4378: The second category relates to the scheduling and acknowledgment scheme of the link, and implies the type of traffic that is supported by the link. These are synchronous, isochronous or asynchronous. There are no specific isochronous links defined, though the default ACL link can be configured to operate in this fashion.
4379: 
4380: -   Synchronous links provide a method of associating the transported data with the Bluetooth piconet clock. This is achieved by reserving regular slots on the physical channel, and transmitting fixed size packets at these regular intervals. Such links are suitable for constant rate isochronous data.
4381:     
4382: -   Asynchronous links provide a method for transporting data that has no time-based characteristics. The data is normally expected to be retransmitted until successfully received, and each data entity can be processed at any time after receipt, without reference to the time of receipt of any previous or successive entity in the stream (providing the ordering of data entities is preserved).
4383:     
4384: -   Isochronous links provide a method for transporting data that has time-based characteristics. The data may be retransmitted until received or expired. The data rate on the link need not be constant (this being the main difference from synchronous links).
4385:     
4386: 
4387: ###### 3.5.3. Class of data
4388: 
4389: The final category is related to the class of data that is carried by the link. This is either control data or user data. The user data category is sub-divided into L2CAP data, stream data, and periodic broadcast data.
4390: 
4391: -   Control links are only used for transporting LMP or Link Layer messages between two Controllers. These links are invisible above the baseband layer or Link Layer and cannot be directly instantiated, configured, or released by applications, other than by the use of the services, such as connection and disconnection, that have this effect implicitly. Control links are always multiplexed with an equivalent L2CAP data link onto a logical transport. For example, ACL-C and ACL-U are multiplexed onto an ACL logical transport, whereas ADVB-C and ADVB-U are multiplexed onto ADVB and PADVB logical transports. Subject to the rules defining the acknowledgment scheme, the control link traffic normally takes priority over the L2CAP link traffic.
4392:     
4393: -   L2CAP links are used to transport L2CAP PDUs, which may carry the L2CAP signaling channel or framed user data submitted to user-instantiated L2CAP channels. L2CAP frames submitted to the baseband may be larger than the available Baseband packets. A link control protocol embedded within the LLID field preserves the frame-start and frame-continuation semantics when the frame is transmitted in a number of fragments to the receiver. Normally, L2CAP links give reliable delivery of data priority over timely delivery.
4394:     
4395: -   Stream links are used to transport user data when timely delivery of the latest data has priority over reliability. Lost data may be replaced by padding at the receiver. On BR/EDR, these links (SCO and eSCO) have a fixed bandwidth and are always bidirectional between two devices; on LE, they have a variable bandwidth with a specified maximum and may be either bidirectional between two devices (CIS) or unidirectional broadcast (BIS).
4396:     
4397: -   Periodic broadcast data is transmitted at regular intervals, possibly with jitter, by a device. It has no acknowledgment mechanism. The same data is transmitted until it is explicitly changed. This is sent on the PBD logical link on BR/EDR and on the ADVB-U logical link on LE.

4400: ###### 3.5.4. Logical transports
4401: 
4402: ###### 3.5.4.1. BR/EDR asynchronous connection-oriented (ACL)
4403: 
4404: The asynchronous connection-oriented (ACL) logical transport is used to carry LMP and L2CAP control signaling and best effort asynchronous user data. The ACL logical transport uses a 1-bit ARQN/SEQN scheme to provide simple channel reliability. Every active Peripheral within a piconet has one ACL logical transport to the piconet Central, known as the default ACL.
4405: 
4406: The default ACL is created between the Central and the Peripheral when a device joins a piconet (connects to the basic piconet physical channel). This default ACL is assigned a logical transport address (LT\_ADDR) by the piconet Central. This LT\_ADDR is also used to identify the active physical link when required (or as a piconet active member identifier, effectively for the same purpose).
4407: 
4408: The LT\_ADDR for the default ACL is reused for synchronous connection-oriented logical transports between the same Central and Peripheral. Thus the LT\_ADDR is not sufficient on its own to identify the default ACL. However the packet types used on the ACL are different from those used on the synchronous connection-oriented logical transport. Therefore, the ACL logical transport can be identified by the LT\_ADDR field in the packet header in combination with the packet type field.
4409: 
4410: The default ACL may be used for isochronous data transport by configuring it to automatically flush packets after the packets have expired. Asynchronous traffic can be sent over an ACL logical transport configured for isochronous traffic by marking the asynchronous packets as non-automatically-flushable. This allows both isochronous and asynchronous traffic to be transferred at the same time to a single device.
4411: 
4412: If the default ACL is removed from the active physical link then all other logical transports that exist between the Central and the Peripheral are also removed. In the case of unexpected loss of synchronization to the piconet physical channel the physical link and all logical transports and logical links cease to exist at the time that this synchronization loss is detected.
4413: 
4414: ###### 3.5.4.2. BR/EDR synchronous connection-oriented (SCO)
4415: 
4416: The synchronous connection-oriented (SCO) logical transport is a symmetric, point-to-point transport between the Central and a specific Peripheral. The SCO logical transport reserves slots on the physical channel and can therefore be considered as a circuit-switched connection between the Central and the Peripheral. SCO logical transports carry 64 kb/s of information synchronized with the piconet clock. Typically this information is an encoded voice stream. Three different SCO configurations exist, offering a balance between robustness, delay and bandwidth consumption.
4417: 
4418: Each SCO-S logical link is supported by a single SCO logical transport, which is assigned the same LT\_ADDR as the default ACL logical transport between the devices. Therefore the LT\_ADDR field is not sufficient to identify the destination of a received packet. Because the SCO links use reserved slots, a device uses a combination of the LT\_ADDR, the slot numbers (a property of the physical channel) and the packet type to identify transmissions on the SCO link.
4419: 
4420: Although slots are reserved for the SCO, it is permissible to use a reserved slot for traffic from another channel that has a higher priority. This may be required as a result of QoS commitments, or to send LMP signaling on the default ACL when the physical channel bandwidth is fully occupied by SCOs. As SCOs carry different packet types to ACLs, the packet type is used to identify SCO traffic (in addition to the slot number and LT\_ADDR).
4421: 
4422: There are no further architectural layers defined by the specification that are transported over a SCO link. A number of standard formats are defined for the 64 kb/s stream that is transported, or an unformatted stream is allowed where the application is responsible for interpreting the encoding of the stream.
4423: 
4424: ###### 3.5.4.3. BR/EDR extended synchronous connection-oriented (eSCO)
4425: 
4426: The extended synchronous connection-oriented (eSCO) logical transport is a symmetric or asymmetric, point-to-point transport between the Central and a specific Peripheral. The eSCO reserves slots on the physical channel and can therefore be considered as a circuit-switched connection between the Central and the Peripheral. eSCO links offer a number of extensions over the standard SCO links, in that they support a more flexible combination of packet types and selectable data contents in the packets and selectable slot periods, allowing a range of synchronous bit rates to be supported.
4427: 
4428: eSCO links also can offer limited retransmission of packets (unlike SCO links where there is no retransmission). If these retransmissions are required they take place in the slots that follow the reserved slots, otherwise the slots may be used for other traffic.
4429: 
4430: Each eSCO-S logical link is supported by a single eSCO logical transport, identified by a LT\_ADDR that is unique within the piconet for the duration of the eSCO. eSCO-S links are created using LM signaling and follow scheduling rules similar to SCO-S links.
4431: 
4432: There are no further architectural layers defined by the specification that are transported over an eSCO-S link. Instead applications may use the data stream for whatever purpose they require, subject to the transport characteristics of the stream being suitable for the data being transported.
4433: 
4434: ###### 3.5.4.4. BR/EDR active Peripheral broadcast (APB)
4435: 
4436: The active Peripheral broadcast logical transport is used to transport LMP control signaling and connectionless L2CAP user traffic to all devices in the piconet that are currently connected to the physical channel that is used by the APB. There is no acknowledgment protocol and the traffic is uni-directional from the piconet Central to the Peripherals. The APB channel may be used for L2CAP group traffic (a legacy of the 1.1 specification), and is never used for L2CAP connection-oriented channels or L2CAP control signaling.
4437: 
4438: The APB logical transport is inherently unreliable because of the lack of acknowledgment. To improve the reliability, each packet is transmitted a number of times. An identical sequence number is used to assist with filtering retransmissions at the Peripheral.
4439: 
4440: The APB logical transport is identified by a reserved LT\_ADDR.
4441: 
4442: An APB is implicitly created whenever a piconet exists, and there is always one APB associated with each of the active physical links (whether operating over the basic or adapted piconet physical channel) that exist within the piconet. Because the basic and adapted piconet physical channels, and different channel maps on the adapted piconet physical channel, are mostly coincident, a Peripheral cannot always distinguish which of the APB channels is being used to transmit the packets. This adds to the general unreliability of the APB channel. (Although it is, perhaps, no more unreliable than general missed packets.)
4443: 
4444: A Central may decide to use only one of its two possible APBs (when it has both a basic and adapted piconet physical channel), or only one of the channel maps in use on the adapted piconet physical channel (when it has more than one map), as with sufficient retransmissions or careful selection of which slots to transmit on it is possible to address all Peripherals.
4445: 
4446: The APB channel is never used to carry L2CAP control signals.

4451: 
4452: The LE asynchronous connection (LE ACL) logical transport is used to carry LL and L2CAP control signaling and best effort asynchronous user data. The LE ACL logical transport uses a 1-bit NESN/SN scheme to provide simple channel reliability. Every active Peripheral has one LE ACL logical transport to the piconet Central, known as the default LE ACL.
4453: 
4454: The default LE ACL is automatically created between the Central and the Peripheral when the piconet connecting them is created. 4478: ###### 3.5.4.7. LE advertising broadcast (ADVB)
4479: 
4480: The LE advertising broadcast logical transport is used to transport broadcast control and user data to all scanning devices in a given area. There is no acknowledgment protocol and the traffic is predominately unidirectional from the advertising device. A scanning device can send requests over the logical transport to get additional broadcast user data, or to form an LE ACL logical transport connection. The LE Advertising Broadcast logical transport data is carried only over the LE advertising broadcast link.
4481: 
4482: The ADVB logical transport is inherently unreliable because of the lack of acknowledgment. To improve the reliability, each packet is transmitted a number of times over the LE advertising broadcast link.

4486: ###### 3.5.4.8. Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast (CPB)
4487: 
4488: The CPB logical transport is used to transport profile broadcast data to all devices connected to the Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast logical transport. There is no acknowledgment scheme and the traffic is unidirectional from a Transmitter to zero or more Receivers. To improve reliability, profile broadcast data may be transmitted multiple times.
4489: 
4490: The CPB logical transport is created on the transmitter whenever the Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast is started. The CPB logical transport is created on the receiver whenever Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast reception is configured. The CPB logical transport is identified by a unique LT\_ADDR within the piconet that is reserved specifically for that purpose by the Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast Transmitter.

4493: 
4494: ###### 3.5.4.9.1. LE periodic advertising broadcast (PADVB)
4495: 
4496: The LE periodic advertising broadcast logical transport is used to transport periodic broadcast control and user data to all scanning devices in a given area. The data may be constant for several periods or may change frequently. There is no acknowledgment protocol and the traffic is unidirectional from the advertising device. The LE Periodic Advertising Broadcast logical transport data is carried only over the LE periodic physical link.
4497: 
4498: The PADVB logical transport is inherently unreliable because of the lack of acknowledgment. To improve the reliability, the period between transmissions can be shorter than the interval between changes to the data so that each packet can be transmitted a number of times over the LE periodic physical link.
4499: 
4500: A PADVB is created whenever an advertising device begins periodic advertising. The PADVB logical transport is identified by the advertiser's Bluetooth Device Address, timing, and advertising set.

4502: ###### 3.5.4.9.2. Periodic advertising with responses (PAwR)
4503: 
4504: The LE periodic advertising with responses logical transport is used to transport periodic broadcast control and user data to all scanning devices in a given area. These broadcasts are grouped into subevents, allowing a subset of the devices to be synchronized with each subevent. Each subevent can then contain information that is directed to the subset of devices synchronized to that subevent. This allows the broadcasting device to send data to many devices and the synchronized devices to only have to listen very infrequently for information directed to them. The data may be constant for several periods or may change frequently. The PAwR logical transport data is carried only over the LE periodic physical link.
4505: 
4506: The PAwR logical transport also includes response slots. The devices that have been directly addressed by the advertising device use response slots to send back responses. A higher layer specification determines the set of devices that can respond and when they respond. The PAwR logical transport is inherently unreliable, but the ability to use response slots allows higher layer acknowledgments to be used to provide reliability.
4507: 
4508: A PAwR logical transport is created whenever an advertising device begins periodic advertising configured to use subevents and responses. The PAwR logical transport is identified by the advertiser's Bluetooth Device Address, timing, and advertising set.

4510: ###### 3.5.4.10. Connected Isochronous Stream (CIS)
4511: 
4512: The CIS is a data-symmetric or data-asymmetric, point-to-point logical transport between the Central and a specific Peripheral. A CIS reserves transmission/reception (Tx/Rx) periods, known as subevents, on the isochronous physical channel and can be considered as a circuit switched connection between the Central and the Peripheral. The CIS supports a variable flushing period for payloads, variable size data contents in the packets, and a variable number of subevents, allowing a range of isochronous data rates, latencies, and re-transmissions to be supported. A CIS can be configured to retransmit packets by providing more subevents than required for transmitting the data. If retransmissions are required, they take place in the subevents (of the current or subsequent events) that follow.
4513: 
4514: Each LE-S or LE-F logical link is supported by a single CIS that is identified by a unique access address for the lifetime of the CIS. The LE-S or LE F links are created by using Link Layer procedures. The higher layer may use the data stream for whatever purpose it requires, as long as the transport characteristics of the stream are suitable for the data that is being transported. All isochronous connections are terminated when the associated LE piconet physical channel is terminated.
4515: 
4516: ###### 3.5.4.11. Connected Isochronous Group (CIG)
4517: 
4518: Each CIS is part of a CIG. A CIG may have one or more CISes, all with the same Central but possibly different Peripherals. Multiple CISes in a CIG have a common timing reference based on the Central timing and are synchronized in time. The common timing reference of multiple CISes helps devices to synchronize their input or output data. For example, when the left and right channels of an audio stereo stream, which are received by separate devices, need to be rendered at the same time. Multiple CISes in a CIG can be scheduled sequentially or in an interleaved arrangement.

4520: ###### 3.5.4.12. Broadcast Isochronous Stream (BIS)
4521: 
4522: The BIS logical transport is used to transport one or more isochronous data streams to all devices for a BIS within range. The data may be fixed or variable size, framed or unframed. A BIS has one or more subevents for transmitting isochronous data packets. A BIS supports transmission of multiple new isochronous data packets in every BIS event. There is no acknowledgment protocol and the traffic is unidirectional from the broadcasting device. The BIS logical transport is inherently unreliable because of the lack of acknowledgment. To improve the reliability of delivery, the isochronous data packets can be unconditionally re-transmitted by increasing the number of subevents in every event. The reliability of delivery can also be improved by transmitting packets in intervals earlier than the intervals they are associated with; this is called "pre-transmission". A BIS supports LE-S or LE-F logical links. A BIS is identified by a unique access address and the timing information. The access address and the timing information is transmitted in the packet that is sent using the associated Periodic Advertising Broadcast (PADVB) logical transport. A scanning device that supports the Synchronized Receiver role feature may receive isochronous data from a BIS after synchronizing to the BIS by using the timing information from the periodic advertising train.

CIS 中的 LE 等时物理信道可用于 LE 微微网中设备之间的一对一通信。中心设备可与 LE 微微网中的外围设备建立一个或多个 CIS；即，LE 等时物理信道可在给定中心设备与外围设备之间承载一个或多个 CIS 逻辑传输。当关联的 LE 微微网物理信道终止时，LE 等时物理信道及其承载的所有 CIS 随之终止。如果中心设备已与多个外围设备建立微微网，则它可同时与其中多个外围设备建立 LE 等时物理信道。

The LE isochronous physical channel can be used for one-to-many communication topologies of unconnected LE devices. Each LE isochronous physical channel can carry one or more BIS logical transports.
LE 等时物理信道可用于未连接 LE 设备之间的一对多通信拓扑。每个 LE 等时物理信道可承载一个或多个 BIS 逻辑传输。

###### 3.3.2.5. LE Channel Sounding physical channel
###### 3.3.2.5. LE 信道探测物理信道

The LE CS physical channel can be created to transfer time and phase information that can be used to generate a distance estimate.
可创建 LE CS 物理信道以传输可用于生成距离估计的时间和相位信息。

###### 3.3.2.5.1. Overview
###### 3.3.2.5.1. 概述

An LE CS physical channel is used to exchange time-interleaved modulated tones and packets that allow a pair of devices to measure the time of flight, amplitude, and phase of signals sent over the communication channel. This information can be used to estimate the distance between two LE devices.
LE CS 物理信道用于交换时间交错的调制音调和分组，使一对设备能够测量通过通信信道发送的信号的飞行时间、幅度和相位。该信息可用于估计两个 LE 设备之间的距离。

###### 3.3.2.5.2. Characteristics
###### 3.3.2.5.2. 特性

The LE CS physical channel is characterized by a pre-negotiated sequence of exchanges that make up a CS procedure. Characteristics and content of these exchanges is derived from the output of a Deterministic Random Bit Generator (DRBG). The DRBG is used to generate the content of the CS Access Address and payload content. It is also used to influence the modulated content of tone transmissions. Finally, the DRBG is used to seed the selection of the pseudo-random sequence of the PHY channels used in the channel hop sequence of a Channel Sounding procedure.
LE CS 物理信道的特征在于构成 CS 过程的预协商交换序列。这些交换的特征和内容源自确定性随机比特发生器（DRBG）的输出。DRBG 用于生成 CS 接入地址的内容和载荷内容，还用于影响音调传输的调制内容。最后，DRBG 用于为信道探测过程的跳频序列中所用 PHY 信道的伪随机序列的选择提供种子。

The duration of a CS procedure is determined by the time it takes for a predetermined number of CS steps to be exchanged. Additional time may be required to partition the CS steps into subevents in order to coexist with other activities using the same radio or spectrum.
CS 过程的持续时间由交换预定数量 CS 步骤所需的时间决定。可能需要额外时间将 CS 步骤划分为子事件，以便与使用同一射频或频谱的其他活动共存。

CS steps are defined as a bidirectional exchange between initiator and reflector devices. These steps are further aggregated into a related timing group known as a CS subevent. These subevents are timed from an offset of the underlying LE piconet physical channel connection event anchor point. A CS event is defined as the group of all CS subevents offset from the same LE piconet physical channel connection event anchor point.
CS 步骤被定义为发起方与反射方设备之间的双向交换。这些步骤进一步聚合为一个相关的定时组，称为 CS 子事件。这些子事件以底层 LE 微微网物理信道连接事件锚点的偏移量来定时。CS 事件被定义为从同一 LE 微微网物理信道连接事件锚点偏移的所有 CS 子事件的分组。

Each step exchange may include a modulated packet, a modulated tone, or both. The initiator device transmits first, followed by at least one transmission from the reflector. A modulated tone may be transmitted more than once in each direction in cases where multiple antenna paths are employed.
每次步骤交换可包括一个调制分组、一个调制音调，或两者兼有。发起方设备首先发送，随后反射方至少进行一次发送。在采用多条天线路径的情况下，调制音调可在每个方向上发送多次。

###### 3.3.2.5.3. Topology
###### 3.3.2.5.3. 拓扑

An LE Channel Sounding physical channel is used for one-to-one communication between two devices that are in the same piconet, where one is in the initiator role and the other is in the reflector role. In the context of CS, an initiator is the device that starts the CS procedure, and a reflector is the device that responds. The procedure's operating parameters are exchanged in Link Layer control messages. LE CS physical channel timing depends on the timing of the initiator device, which is followed by the reflector device. The LE Central device may assume either the initiator or reflector role. Likewise, the LE Peripheral device may assume either role.
LE 信道探测物理信道用于同一微微网中两个设备之间的一对一通信，其中一个处于发起方角色，另一个处于反射方角色。在 CS 语境中，发起方是启动 CS 过程的设备，反射方是作出响应的设备。该过程的操作参数通过链路层控制消息交换。LE CS 物理信道的定时取决于发起方设备的定时，反射方设备随后跟随。LE 中心设备可承担发起方或反射方中的任一角色。同样，LE 外围设备也可承担任一角色。

An LE device can use only one LE Channel Sounding physical channel at a time. To support multiple concurrent Channel Sounding operations, the device uses time-division multiplexing between multiple LE Channel Sounding physical channels, which allows a device to appear to support multiple connected devices with Channel Sounding physical channels.
一个 LE 设备一次只能使用一个 LE 信道探测物理信道。为支持多个并发的信道探测操作，设备在多个 LE 信道探测物理信道之间使用时分复用，这使设备能够表现为支持多个具有信道探测物理信道的已连接设备。

##### 3.4. Physical links
##### 3.4. 物理链路

A physical link represents a baseband connection between Bluetooth devices. A physical link is always associated with exactly one physical channel (although a physical channel may support more than one physical link). Within the Bluetooth system a physical link is a virtual concept that has no direct representation within the structure of a transmitted packet.
物理链路表示蓝牙设备之间的基带连接。一条物理链路总是恰好与一个物理信道相关联（尽管一个物理信道可支持多条物理链路）。在蓝牙系统中，物理链路是一个虚拟概念，在所发送分组的结构中没有直接表示。

In BR/EDR the access code packet field, together with the clock and address of the Central Bluetooth device, is used to identify a physical channel. In LE, the access address and channel map, including *hopIncrement* in the case of Channel Selection Algorithm #1 or an event counter in the case of Channel Selection Algorithm #2, are used to identify a physical channel. For BR/EDR and LE, there is no subsequent part of the packet that directly identifies the physical link. Instead, the physical link may be identified by association with the logical transport, as each logical transport is only received on one physical link.
在 BR/EDR 中，接入码分组字段与中心蓝牙设备的时钟和地址一起用于标识一个物理信道。在 LE 中，接入地址和信道映射（在信道选择算法 #1 的情况下包括 *hopIncrement*，在信道选择算法 #2 的情况下包括事件计数器）用于标识一个物理信道。对于 BR/EDR 和 LE，分组中没有任何后续部分直接标识物理链路。相反，物理链路可通过与逻辑传输的关联来标识，因为每个逻辑传输仅在一个物理链路上被接收。

Some physical link types have properties that may be modified. An example of this is the transmit power for the link. Other physical link types have no modifiable properties. In the case of BR/EDR physical links with modifiable properties the LM protocol is used to adapt these properties. In the case of LE physical links with modifiable properties the LL protocol is used to adapt these properties. As the LM protocol (BR/EDR) or LL protocol (LE) is supported at a higher layer (by a logical link) the appropriate physical link is identified by implication from the logical link that transports the LM or LL signaling.
某些物理链路类型具有可修改的属性。链路的发射功率即是此类属性的一个示例。其他物理链路类型没有可修改的属性。对于具有可修改属性的 BR/EDR 物理链路，使用 LM 协议来调整这些属性。对于具有可修改属性的 LE 物理链路，使用 LL 协议来调整这些属性。由于 LM 协议（BR/EDR）或 LL 协议（LE）在更高层（由逻辑链路）支持，因此适当的物理链路由承送 LM 或 LL 信令的逻辑链路隐含地标识。

In the situation where a transmission is broadcast over a number of different physical links, then the transmission parameters are selected to be suitable for all of the physical links.
当一次传输在多条不同物理链路上广播时，传输参数的选择应适合所有这些物理链路。

###### 3.4.1. BR/EDR links supported by the basic and adapted piconet physical channels
###### 3.4.1. 由基本和适配微微网物理信道支持的 BR/EDR 链路

The basic piconet physical channel supports a physical link which may only be active. The adapted piconet physical channel may support several physical links, including active and Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast. An active physical link is a point-to-point link between the Central and a Peripheral. A Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast physical link is a point-to-multipoint link between the Transmitter (Central) and zero or more Receivers (Peripherals). At least one physical link on the piconet physical channel is always present when a Peripheral is synchronized in the piconet.
基本微微网物理信道支持一条只能为活动的物理链路。适配微微网物理信道可支持多条物理链路，包括活动链路和无连接外围广播（Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast）链路。活动物理链路是中心设备与外围设备之间的点对点链路。无连接外围广播物理链路是发送器（中心设备）与零个或多个接收器（外围设备）之间的点对多点链路。当外围设备在微微网中同步时，微微网物理信道上至少存在一条物理链路。

###### 3.4.1.1. Active physical link
###### 3.4.1.1. 活动物理链路

The physical link between a Central and a Peripheral is active if a default ACL logical transport exists between the devices. Active physical links have no direct identification of their own, but are identified by association with the default ACL logical transport ID with which there is a one-to-one correspondence.
如果中心设备与外围设备之间存在默认 ACL 逻辑传输，则它们之间的物理链路为活动的。活动物理链路没有自身的直接标识，而是通过与默认 ACL 逻辑传输 ID 的关联来标识，二者之间存在一一对应关系。

An active physical link has the associated property of radio transmit power in each direction. Transmissions from Peripherals are always directed over the active physical link to the Central, and use the transmit power that is a property of this link in the Peripheral to Central direction. Transmissions from the Central may be directed over a single active physical link (to a specific Peripheral) or over a number of physical links (to a group of Peripherals in the piconet). In the case of point-to-point transmissions the Central uses the appropriate transmit power for the physical link in question. (In the case of point-to-multipoint transmissions the Central uses a transmit power appropriate for the set of devices addressed.)
活动物理链路在每个方向上具有关联的射频发射功率属性。来自外围设备的传输总是通过活动物理链路定向到中心设备，并使用作为该链路在外围设备到中心设备方向属性的那个发射功率。来自中心设备的传输可在单条活动物理链路上（定向到特定外围设备）或在多条物理链路上（定向到微微网中的一组外围设备）进行。在点对点传输的情况下，中心设备使用适合该物理链路的发射功率。（在点对多点传输的情况下，中心设备使用适合所寻址设备集合的发射功率。）

Active physical links may be placed into Hold or Sniff mode. The effect of these modes is to modify the periods when the physical link is active and may carry traffic. Logical transports that have defined scheduling characteristics are not affected by these modes and continue according to their pre-defined scheduling behavior. The default ACL logical transport and other links with undefined scheduling characteristics are subject to the mode of the active physical link.
活动物理链路可被置于保持（Hold）或嗅探（Sniff）模式。这些模式的作用是修改物理链路处于活动状态并可承送业务的时间段。具有已定义调度特性的逻辑传输不受这些模式影响，并按其预定义的调度行为继续运行。默认 ACL 逻辑传输及其他具有未定义调度特性的链路则受活动物理链路模式的约束。

###### 3.4.1.2. \[本节不再使用\]

###### 3.4.1.3. Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast physical link
###### 3.4.1.3. 无连接外围广播物理链路

A Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast physical link is present on a Receiver (Peripheral) when it is synchronized in the piconet where a CPB logical transport exists. On a Transmitter (Central), a Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast physical link is present when a CPB logical transport exists whether or not any Receivers are synchronized. The Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast physical link is a point-to-multipoint unidirectional link between a Transmitter and zero or more Receivers.
当接收器（外围设备）在存在 CPB 逻辑传输的微微网中同步时，其上存在无连接外围广播物理链路。在发送器（中心设备）上，只要存在 CPB 逻辑传输，无论是否有接收器同步，都存在无连接外围广播物理链路。无连接外围广播物理链路是发送器与零个或多个接收器之间的点对多点单向链路。

Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast physical links do not support power control because there is no feedback from Receivers to the Transmitter. Traffic is always directed from a single Transmitter to zero or more Receivers.
无连接外围广播物理链路不支持功率控制，因为不存在从接收器到发送器的反馈。业务总是从单个发送器定向到零个或多个接收器。

Connectionless Peripheral Broadcast packets are sent at regular intervals. The BR/EDR Controller selects an interval within a range requested by the Host.
无连接外围广播分组以固定间隔发送。BR/EDR 控制器在主机请求的范围内选择一个间隔。

###### 3.4.2. BR/EDR links supported by the scanning physical channels
###### 3.4.2. 由扫描物理信道支持的 BR/EDR 链路

In the case of inquiry scan and page scan channels, the physical link exists for a relatively short time and cannot be controlled or modified in any way. These types of physical links are not further elaborated.
对于查询扫描和寻呼扫描信道，物理链路存在的时间相对较短，且不能以任何方式控制或修改。这些类型的物理链路不再进一步阐述。

###### 3.4.3. LE links supported by the LE physical channels
###### 3.4.3. 由 LE 物理信道支持的 LE 链路

The LE piconet physical channels support an LE active physical link. The physical link is a point-to-point link between the Central and a Peripheral. It is always present when the Peripheral is in a connection with the Central.
LE 微微网物理信道支持 LE 活动物理链路。该物理链路是中心设备与外围设备之间的点对点链路。当外围设备与中心设备连接时，它总是存在。

The LE advertising physical channels support an LE advertising physical link. The physical link is a broadcast between the advertiser device and one or more scanner or initiator devices. It is always present when the advertiser is broadcasting advertisement events.
LE 广播物理信道支持 LE 广播物理链路。该物理链路是广播器设备与一个或多个扫描器或发起器设备之间的广播。当广播器正在广播广播事件时，它总是存在。

The LE periodic physical channels support an LE periodic physical link. The physical link is a broadcast between the advertiser device and one or more scanner devices. It is always present when the advertiser is broadcasting periodic advertising events.
LE 周期性物理信道支持 LE 周期性物理链路。该物理链路是广播器设备与一个或多个扫描器设备之间的广播。当广播器正在广播周期性广播事件时，它总是存在。

The LE isochronous physical channels support LE isochronous physical links. An LE isochronous physical link can be a point-to-point link between a Central and a Peripheral or a connectionless link between a broadcast isochronous transmitter and multiple receiving devices.
LE 等时物理信道支持 LE 等时物理链路。LE 等时物理链路可以是中心设备与外围设备之间的点对点链路，或是广播等时发送器与多个接收设备之间的无连接链路。

###### 3.4.3.1. Active physical link
###### 3.4.3.1. 活动物理链路

The physical link between a Central and a Peripheral is active if a default LE ACL logical transport exists between the devices. Active physical links are each associated with a separate piconet physical channel, which in turn is identified by the randomly generated Access Address used in the Link Layer packet. Each Access Address has a one-to-one relationship with the Central and the Peripheral of the active physical link.
如果中心设备与外围设备之间存在默认 LE ACL 逻辑传输，则它们之间的物理链路为活动的。每条活动物理链路各自与一条独立的微微网物理信道相关联，而该信道又由链路层分组中使用的随机生成的接入地址标识。每个接入地址与该活动物理链路的中心设备和外围设备具有一一对应关系。

An active physical link has the associated property of radio transmit power in each direction, which may be different in each direction. A device uses the appropriate transmit power for the physical link in question.
活动物理链路在每个方向上具有关联的射频发射功率属性，且每个方向可能不同。设备使用适合该物理链路的发射功率。

###### 3.4.3.2. Advertising physical link
###### 3.4.3.2. 广播物理链路

An advertising physical link between an advertising device and an initiating device for the purposes of forming a connection (active physical link) can exist for a relatively short period of time. These advertising physical links cannot be controlled or modified in any way and these types of physical links are not further elaborated.
为建立连接（活动物理链路）而在广播设备与发起设备之间存在的广播物理链路可能存在相对较短的时间。这些广播物理链路不能以任何方式控制或修改，这些类型的物理链路不再进一步阐述。

An advertising physical link between an advertising device and a scanning device used for periodic broadcasting of user data can exist for longer periods of time. There is no identification information about the physical link within the protocol. The relationship between the advertising and scanning device is established through the use of the Bluetooth Device Address.
用于周期性广播用户数据的广播设备与扫描设备之间的广播物理链路可存在较长时间。协议中没有关于该物理链路的标识信息。广播设备与扫描设备之间的关系通过使用蓝牙设备地址来建立。

###### 3.4.3.3. Periodic physical link
###### 3.4.3.3. 周期性物理链路

A periodic physical link between an advertising device and one or more scanning devices normally exists for a prolonged period of time. Periodic physical links are each associated with a separate periodic physical channel, which in turn is identified by the randomly generated Access Address used in the Link Layer packet. Each Access Address has a one-to-one relationship with the advertiser of the periodic physical link.
广播设备与一个或多个扫描设备之间的周期性物理链路通常存在较长时间。每条周期性物理链路各自与一条独立的周期性物理信道相关联，而该信道又由链路层分组中使用的随机生成的接入地址标识。每个接入地址与该周期性物理链路的广播器具有一一对应关系。

###### 3.4.3.4. Isochronous physical links
###### 3.4.3.4. 等时物理链路

The isochronous physical link uses an isochronous physical channel and carries CIS and BIS logical transports.
等时物理链路使用等时物理信道并承载 CIS 和 BIS 逻辑传输。

Isochronous physical links carrying CIS(es) use the appropriate transmit power level for the physical link in question. Devices use power control on the associated ACL-C logical link to adapt the transmit power level for the physical link.
承载 CIS 的等时物理链路使用适合该物理链路的发射功率电平。设备在关联的 ACL-C 逻辑链路上使用功率控制来调整该物理链路的发射功率电平。

Isochronous physical links carrying BIS(es) do not support power control because there is no feedback from Observers to the Broadcaster. Traffic is always directed from a single Broadcaster to zero or more Observers.
承载 BIS 的等时物理链路不支持功率控制，因为不存在从观察者到广播器的反馈。业务总是从单个广播器定向到零个或多个观察者。

###### 3.4.3.5. Channel Sounding physical link
###### 3.4.3.5. 信道探测物理链路

Channel Sounding procedures exist within an LE Channel Sounding physical link and are characterized by their transitory existence as well as their unique timing characteristics relative to an LE active physical link. Channel Sounding procedures are based on a preexisting LE active physical link. A CS procedure's start timing is also dependent on the timing of the corresponding LE active physical link.
信道探测过程存在于 LE 信道探测物理链路内，其特征在于其短暂的存在以及相对于 LE 活动物理链路的独特定时特性。信道探测过程基于已存在的 LE 活动物理链路。CS 过程的开始定时也取决于对应 LE 活动物理链路的定时。

A Channel Sounding physical channel supports a Channel Sounding physical link.
信道探测物理信道支持一条信道探测物理链路。

##### 3.5. Logical links and logical transports
##### 3.5. 逻辑链路与逻辑传输

A variety of logical links are available to support different application data transport requirements. Each logical link is associated with a logical transport, which has a number of characteristics. These characteristics include flow control, acknowledgment/repeat mechanisms, sequence numbering and scheduling behavior. Logical transports are able to carry different types of logical links (depending on the type of the logical transport). In the case of some of the Bluetooth logical links these are multiplexed onto the same logical transport. Logical transports may be carried by active physical links on either the basic or the adapted piconet physical channel.

This allows both isochronous and asynchronous traffic to be transferred at the same time to a single device.
默认 ACL 可用于等时数据传输，方法是将其配置为在分组过期后自动刷新分组。通过将异步分组标记为非自动可刷新，异步业务可在配置用于等时业务的 ACL 逻辑传输上发送。这允许等时和异步业务同时传输到单个设备。

If the default ACL is removed from the active physical link then all other logical transports that exist between the Central and the Peripheral are also removed. In the case of unexpected loss of synchronization to the piconet physical channel the physical link and all logical transports and logical links cease to exist at the time that this synchronization loss is detected.
如果默认 ACL 从活动物理链路上被移除，则中心设备与外围设备之间存在的所有其他逻辑传输也将被移除。在意外丢失与微微网物理信道同步的情况下，物理链路以及所有逻辑传输和逻辑链路在检测到该同步丢失时即不复存在。

###### 3.5.4.2. BR/EDR synchronous connection-oriented (SCO)
###### 3.5.4.2. BR/EDR 同步面向连接（SCO）

The synchronous connection-oriented (SCO) logical transport is a symmetric, point-to-point transport between the Central and a specific Peripheral. The SCO logical transport reserves slots on the physical channel and can therefore be considered as a circuit-switched connection between the Central and the Peripheral. SCO logical transports carry 64 kb/s of information synchronized with the piconet clock. Typically this information is an encoded voice stream. Three different SCO configurations exist, offering a balance between robustness, delay and bandwidth consumption.
同步面向连接（SCO）逻辑传输是中心设备与特定外围设备之间的对称、点对点传输。SCO 逻辑传输在物理信道上预留时隙，因此可被视为中心设备与外围设备之间的电路交换连接。SCO 逻辑传输承送与微微网时钟同步的 64 kb/s 信息。该信息通常是已编码的语音流。存在三种不同的 SCO 配置，在鲁棒性、时延和带宽消耗之间提供平衡。

Each SCO-S logical link is supported by a single SCO logical transport, which is assigned the same LT\_ADDR as the default ACL logical transport between the devices. Therefore the LT\_ADDR field is not sufficient to identify the destination of a received packet. Because the SCO links use reserved slots, a device uses a combination of the LT\_ADDR, the slot numbers (a property of the physical channel) and the packet type to identify transmissions on the SCO link.
每条 SCO-S 逻辑链路由单个 SCO 逻辑传输支持，该传输被分配与设备之间默认 ACL 逻辑传输相同的 LT\_ADDR。因此，LT\_ADDR 字段不足以标识接收分组的目的地。由于 SCO 链路使用预留时隙，设备使用 LT\_ADDR、时隙号（物理信道的一个属性）和分组类型的组合来标识 SCO 链路上的传输。

Although slots are reserved for the SCO, it is permissible to use a reserved slot for traffic from another channel that has a higher priority. This may be required as a result of QoS commitments, or to send LMP signaling on the default ACL when the physical channel bandwidth is fully occupied by SCOs. As SCOs carry different packet types to ACLs, the packet type is used to identify SCO traffic (in addition to the slot number and LT\_ADDR).
尽管时隙为 SCO 预留，但允许将预留时隙用于来自具有更高优先级的另一信道的业务。这可能是由于 QoS 承诺所需，或在物理信道带宽被 SCO 完全占用时在默认 ACL 上发送 LMP 信令所需。由于 SCO 承送的分组类型与 ACL 不同，分组类型用于标识 SCO 业务（除时隙号和 LT\_ADDR 之外）。

There are no further architectural layers defined by the specification that are transported over a SCO link. A number of standard formats are defined for the 64 kb/s stream that is transported, or an unformatted stream is allowed where the application is responsible for interpreting the encoding of the stream.
规范未定义在 SCO 链路上传输的进一步架构层。为所传输的 64 kb/s 流定义了若干标准格式，或者允许使用未格式化的流，此时由应用负责解释该流的编码。

###### 3.5.4.3. BR/EDR extended synchronous connection-oriented (eSCO)
###### 3.5.4.3. BR/EDR 扩展同步面向连接（eSCO）

The extended synchronous connection-oriented (eSCO) logical transport is a symmetric or asymmetric, point-to-point transport between the Central and a specific Peripheral. The eSCO reserves slots on the physical channel and can therefore be considered as a circuit-switched connection between the Central and the Peripheral. eSCO links offer a number of extensions over the standard SCO links, in that they support a more flexible combination of packet types and selectable data contents in the packets and selectable slot periods, allowing a range of synchronous bit rates to be supported.
扩展同步面向连接（eSCO）逻辑传输是中心设备与特定外围设备之间的对称或不对称、点对点传输。eSCO 在物理信道上预留时隙，因此可被视为中心设备与外围设备之间的电路交换连接。eSCO 链路相对于标准 SCO 链路提供了若干扩展，即它们支持更灵活的分组类型组合、分组中可选的数据内容以及可选的时隙周期，从而允许支持一定范围的同步比特率。

eSCO links also can offer limited retransmission of packets (unlike SCO links where there is no retransmission). If these retransmissions are required they take place in the slots that follow the reserved slots, otherwise the slots may be used for other traffic.
eSCO 链路还可提供有限的分组重传（不同于没有重传的 SCO 链路）。如果需要这些重传，它们在预留时隙之后的时隙中进行，否则这些时隙可用于其他业务。

Each eSCO-S logical link is supported by a single eSCO logical transport, identified by a LT\_ADDR that is unique within the piconet for the duration of the eSCO. eSCO-S links are created using LM signaling and follow scheduling rules similar to SCO-S links.
每条 eSCO-S 逻辑链路由单个 eSCO 逻辑传输支持，由在 eSCO 持续期间内在微微网内唯一的 LT\_ADDR 标识。eSCO-S 链路使用 LM 信令创建，并遵循与 SCO-S 链路类似的调度规则。

There are no further architectural layers defined by the specification that are transported over an eSCO-S link. Instead applications may use the data stream for whatever purpose they require, subject to the transport characteristics of the stream being suitable for the data being transported.
规范未定义在 eSCO-S 链路上传输的进一步架构层。相反，应用可出于其所需的任何目的使用该数据流，前提是该流的传输特性适合所传输的数据。

###### 3.5.4.4. BR/EDR active Peripheral broadcast (APB)
###### 3.5.4.4. BR/EDR 活动外围广播（APB）

The active Peripheral broadcast logical transport is used to transport LMP control signaling and connectionless L2CAP user traffic to all devices in the piconet that are currently connected to the physical channel that is used by the APB. There is no acknowledgment protocol and the traffic is uni-directional from the piconet Central to the Peripherals. The APB channel may be used for L2CAP group traffic (a legacy of the 1.1 specification), and is never used for L2CAP connection-oriented channels or L2CAP control signaling.
活动外围广播逻辑传输用于向微微网中当前连接到 APB 所用物理信道的所有设备承送 LMP 控制信令和无连接 L2CAP 用户业务。没有确认协议，且业务是从微微网中心设备到外围设备的单向业务。APB 信道可用于 L2CAP 组业务（1.1 规范的遗留特性），但从不用于 L2CAP 面向连接信道或 L2CAP 控制信令。

The APB logical transport is inherently unreliable because of the lack of acknowledgment. To improve the reliability, each packet is transmitted a number of times. An identical sequence number is used to assist with filtering retransmissions at the Peripheral.
由于缺乏确认，APB 逻辑传输本质上不可靠。为提高可靠性，每个分组被发送多次。使用相同的序号以辅助在外围设备处过滤重传。

The APB logical transport is identified by a reserved LT\_ADDR.
APB 逻辑传输由一个保留的 LT\_ADDR 标识。

An APB is implicitly created whenever a piconet exists, and there is always one APB associated with each of the active physical links (whether operating over the basic or adapted piconet physical channel) that exist within the piconet. Because the basic and adapted piconet physical channels, and different channel maps on the adapted piconet physical channel, are mostly coincident, a Peripheral cannot always distinguish which of the APB channels is being used to transmit the packets. This adds to the general unreliability of the APB channel. (Although it is, perhaps, no more unreliable than general missed packets.)
每当微微网存在时就隐式创建一个 APB，并且微微网内存在的每条活动物理链路（无论是在基本还是适配微微网物理信道上运行）总是关联一个 APB。由于基本和适配微微网物理信道以及适配微微网物理信道上的不同信道映射大部分重合，外围设备并不总能区分正在使用哪个 APB 信道来发送分组。这增加了 APB 信道的一般不可靠性。（尽管它或许并不比一般的分组丢失更不可靠。）

A Central may decide to use only one of its two possible APBs (when it has both a basic and adapted piconet physical channel), or only one of the channel maps in use on the adapted piconet physical channel (when it has more than one map), as with sufficient retransmissions or careful selection of which slots to transmit on it is possible to address all Peripherals.
中心设备可决定仅使用其两个可能的 APB 之一（当它同时具有基本和适配微微网物理信道时），或仅使用适配微微网物理信道上正在使用的信道映射之一（当它具有多于一个映射时），因为通过足够的重传或仔细选择在哪些时隙上发送，可以寻址所有外围设备。

The APB channel is never used to carry L2CAP control signals.
APB 信道从不用于承送 L2CAP 控制信号。

###### 3.5.4.6. LE asynchronous connection (LE ACL)
###### 3.5.4.6. LE 异步连接（LE ACL）

The LE asynchronous connection (LE ACL) logical transport is used to carry LL and L2CAP control signaling and best effort asynchronous user data. The LE ACL logical transport uses a 1-bit NESN/SN scheme to provide simple channel reliability. Every active Peripheral has one LE ACL logical transport to the piconet Central, known as the default LE ACL.
LE 异步连接（LE ACL）逻辑传输用于承送 LL 和 L2CAP 控制信令以及尽力而为的异步用户数据。LE ACL 逻辑传输使用 1 比特的 NESN/SN 方案来提供简单的信道可靠性。每个活动外围设备都有一条到微微网中心设备的 LE ACL 逻辑传输，称为默认 LE ACL。

The default LE ACL is automatically created between the Central and the Peripheral when the piconet connecting them is created. This default LE ACL is assigned an Access Address by the piconet Central. This Access Address is also used to identify the active physical link and active piconet physical channel when required.
当连接中心设备与外围设备的微微网创建时，在二者之间自动创建默认 LE ACL。该默认 LE ACL 由微微网中心设备分配一个接入地址。该接入地址在需要时也用于标识活动物理链路和活动微微网物理信道。

If the default LE ACL is removed from the LE active physical link then all other LE logical transports that exist between the Central and the Peripheral are also removed. In the case of unexpected loss of synchronization to the LE piconet physical channel the LE physical link and all LE logical transports and LE logical links cease to exist at the time that this synchronization loss is detected.
如果默认 LE ACL 从 LE 活动物理链路上被移除，则中心设备与外围设备之间存在的所有其他 LE 逻辑传输也将被移除。在意外丢失与 LE 微微网物理信道同步的情况下，LE 物理链路以及所有 LE 逻辑传输和 LE 逻辑链路在检测到该同步丢失时即不复存在。

The default LE ACL can carry flushable data by configuring the default LE ACL with an ACL Flush Timeout. The ACL Flush Timeout only affects packets that the Host marks as flushable, in which case these packets are removed from the transmission queue when their flush timers expire if they have not yet begun their transmission over the air. LE ACL traffic not marked as flushable is not affected by the ACL Flush Timeout.
默认 LE ACL 可承送可刷新数据，方法是为默认 LE ACL 配置一个 ACL 刷新超时。ACL 刷新超时仅影响主机标记为可刷新的分组，在这种情况下，如果这些分组尚未开始空口传输，则当其刷新定时器到期时它们会从传输队列中移除。未标记为可刷新的 LE ACL 业务不受 ACL 刷新超时影响。

[Figure 3.9](architecture.html#UUID-14ad228c-cbde-41ec-cf36-2860dd5aa240_figure-idm234931142921595 "Figure 3.9: Example of a Host sending flushable data to the Controller") shows an example of a Host sending LE L2CAP PDUs which are marked as flushable. In this example, the Controller Connection Event Interval is lower than the Host interval in which the Host generates new L2CAP PDUs. In this example, the ACL Flush Timeout is set to a value that is lower than the Host interval. PDUs that remain longer than the length of the ACL Flush Timeout in the Controller buffers because of Link Layer delays are flushed before their first transmit opportunity and are not transmitted by the Link Layer, while newer L2CAP PDUs are sent instead at the Host interval rate. In [Figure 3.9](architecture.html#UUID-14ad228c-cbde-41ec-cf36-2860dd5aa240_figure-idm234931142921595 "Figure 3.9: Example of a Host sending flushable data to the Controller"), ACL packet 3 was being retransmitted across multiple connection events, due to interference, while the Host submitted new L2CAP PDUs. L2CAP packets 4 and 5 exceeded their ACL Flush Timeout before their first transmit opportunity and therefore were flushed. When ACL packet 3 was finally acknowledged, newer L2CAP packets 6 and 7 were transmitted as their ACL Flush Timeout had not expired.
[图 3.9](architecture.html#UUID-14ad228c-cbde-41ec-cf36-2860dd5aa240_figure-idm234931142921595 "图 3.9：主机向控制器发送可刷新数据的示例")展示了一个主机发送标记为可刷新的 LE L2CAP PDU 的示例。在此示例中，控制器连接事件间隔低于主机生成新 L2CAP PDU 的主机间隔。在此示例中，ACL 刷新超时被设置为低于主机间隔的值。由于链路层时延而在控制器缓冲区中停留时间超过 ACL 刷新超时长度时的 PDU，在其首次发送机会之前被刷新，且不被链路层发送，而较新的 L2CAP PDU 则以主机间隔速率发送。在[图 3.9](architecture.html#UUID-14ad228c-cbde-41ec-cf36-2860dd5aa240_figure-idm234931142921595 "图 3.9：主机向控制器发送可刷新数据的示例")中，由于干扰，ACL 分组 3 在多个连接事件间被重传，同时主机提交了新的 L2CAP PDU。L2CAP 分组 4 和 5 在其首次发送机会之前超过了其 ACL 刷新超时，因此被刷新。当 ACL 分组 3 最终被确认时，较新的 L2CAP 分组 6 和 7 被发送，因为其 ACL 刷新超时尚未到期。
